rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The opening expression about being among his people has vocalized variants and denotes his clan.
rows.anchor: جاءنا في ظهرته - بالضم وبالكسر وبالتحريكن وظاهرته , أي عشيرته .

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the fighting, the discourse turns from the more important call to consider the afterlife to worldly consequences of that violence.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر القتال وأتبعه ما هو الأهم من أمره بالنظر إلى الآخرة , ذكر ما تسبب عنه من أحوال الدنيا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses is afraid in the city where he killed the man, constantly looking around in fear of someone arriving.
rows.anchor: أي التي قتل القتيل فيها

rows.speaker: البغوي
rows.claim: Al-Baghawi defines watchfulness here as waiting for something feared.
rows.anchor: قال البغوي : والترقب : انتظار المكروه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite who had sought Moses’ help the previous day cries for help again against another Copt who is oppressing him.
rows.anchor: يطلب ما يزيل ما يصرخ بسببه نم الضر من قبطي آخر كان يظلمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses calls the Israelite plainly astray because yesterday’s killing did not deter him from quarreling with someone he could not withstand.
rows.anchor: اي صاحب ضلال بالغ { مبين * } أي واضح الضلال غير خفيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses then comes near the two men to help the Israelite, immediately moving to answer his renewed cry.
rows.anchor: مشيرا بالفاء إلى المبادرة إلى إصراخه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The infinitival particle أن is retained to reinforce the sense of intention; Moses’ movement confirms that he meant to act.
rows.anchor: الحرف الذي أصله المصدر تأكيدا لمعنى الإرادة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses intends to seize the Egyptian forcefully to free the Israelite from him.
rows.anchor: أي موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام { بالذي هو عدو لهما } أي من القبط بأخذه بعنف وسطوة لخلاص الإسرائيلي منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The one described as enemy to both is the Copt who is oppressing the Israelite.
rows.anchor: من القبط بأخذه بعنف وسطوة لخلاص الإسرائيلي منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite, not the Copt, speaks the accusation; the context shows he alone knew Moses had entered unseen by others.
rows.anchor: بدخول المدينة على حين غفلة من أنهم لم يره أحد غير الإسرائيلي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Seeing Moses approach angry and rebuke him, the Israelite assumes Moses means to attack him rather than his Coptic enemy.
rows.anchor: ظانا أنه ما دنا إلا يريد البطش به هو

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He names Moses directly to remove ambiguity while denouncing what he thinks is an objectionable attack.
rows.anchor: باسمه العلم دفعا لكل لبس منكر الفعلة الذي اعتقده

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: By revealing knowledge only he possessed, the Israelite exposes Moses’ secret and intensifies the danger and accusation against him.
rows.anchor: ولما نم عليه وأفشى ما لا يعلمه غيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Here إن means ما, so the accusation means that Moses wants nothing except to become a tyrant.
rows.anchor: أي ما { تريد إلا أن تكون } أي كونا راسخا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Jabbār describes one who dominates and overpowers others.
rows.anchor: أي كونا راسخا { جبارا } اي قاهرا غالبا

rows.speaker: أبو حيان
rows.claim: Abu Hayyan says a tyrant’s characteristic is killing without right.
rows.anchor: قال أبو حيان : وشأن الجبار أن يقتل بغير حق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The accusation portrays Moses as seeking to rule where no one stands above him.
rows.anchor: أي التي تكون بها فلا يكون فوقك أحد

words: وَمَا تُرِيدُ أَن تَكُونَ مِنَ ٱلْمُصْلِحِينَ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The Israelite denies that Moses is naturally among those who make peace, since a peacemaker would not kill in this way.
rows.anchor: فإن المصلح بين الناس لا يصل إلى القتل على هذه الصورة

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: A report from Ibn Abbas says that even a king partial to his people should not punish without proof; Pharaoh had asked whether there was evidence against Moses.
rows.anchor: كما ذكر ذلك في حديث المفتون الذي رواه أبو يعلى عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After Moses killed the Copt, Egyptians suspected the Israelites; the Israelite’s disclosure made Moses’ involvement certain.
rows.anchor: وكانوا - لما قتل ذلك القبطي - ظنوا في بني إسرائيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wording places the subject before the phrase describing his arrival because the moment is grave; the order differs in Yasin.
rows.anchor: قدم فاعل المجيء على متعلقه بخلاف ما في سورة يس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man who comes is one who loves Moses.
rows.anchor: ممن يجب موسى عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He comes from the city’s farthest edge, taking a shortcut and running so quickly that he outruns the others.
rows.anchor: أنه كان ماشيا بقوله : { يسهى } ولكنه اختصر طريقا واسرع في مشيته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The episode demonstrates divine power to take someone into dire danger and then bring sudden relief.
rows.anchor: من الأخذ بالخناق حتى يقول القائل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Calling Moses by name conveys affection and removes any uncertainty about whom he is addressing.
rows.anchor: مناديا له باسمه تعطفا وإزالة للبس

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The malāʾ are the Coptic nobles who hold authority to decide and command.
rows.anchor: أشراف القبط في أيديهم الحل والعقد , لأن لهم القدرة على الأمر والنهي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They are consulting about Moses until each commands the others and takes up their decision.
rows.anchor: حتى وصل حالهم في تشاورهم إلى أن كلا منهم يأمر الآخر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their purpose is to kill Moses because they have heard that he killed one of their people.
rows.anchor: لأنهم سمعوا أنك قتلت صاحبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning means Moses must leave this city.
rows.anchor: أي من هذه المدينة ؛ ثم علل ذلك بقوله على سبيل التأكيد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The man stresses that he is Moses’ sincere adviser to dispel any thought that danger is unlikely because Moses is favored by the king.
rows.anchor: على سبيل التأكيد ليزيل ما يطرق من احتمال عدم القتل لكونه عزيزا عند الملك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses promptly leaves the city after recognizing the man’s warning as credible from its surrounding signs.
rows.anchor: مبادرا { منها } أي المدية لما علم من صدق قوله مما حفه من القرائن

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He fears Pharaoh’s people and repeatedly turns to see whether anyone is following him.
rows.anchor: في الجهات ينظر هلى يتبعه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses addresses God as the benefactor who created and nurtured him and bestowed many kinds of kindness.
rows.anchor: ايها المحسن إلي بالإيجاد والتربية وغير ذلك من وجوه البر

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Najjinī means rescue me; the word derives from najwa, a high place inaccessible to everyone.
rows.anchor: أي خلصني , مشتق من النجوة , وهو المكان العالي الذي لا يصل إليه كل أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The wrongdoers invert proper order by killing the undeserving despite their own power.
rows.anchor: الذين يضعون الأمور في غير مواضعاها فيقتلون من لا يستحق القتل مع قوتهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God answers by directing Moses toward Midian along the main road; his pursuers miss him because they assume a fugitive would use side routes or cross-country paths.
rows.anchor: فاستجاب الله له فوفقه لسلوك الطريق الأعظم نحو مدين , فكان ذلك سبب نجاته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses turns his face toward Midian and sets out intending to reach it, while directing his heart toward God.
rows.anchor: مدينة نبي الله شعيب عليه الصلاة والسللام متوجها بقلبه إلى ربه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: ʿAsā here means fitting, worthy, and assuredly possible.
rows.anchor: { عسى } اي خليق وجدير وحقيق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses places Rabb first because his care and watchfulness toward God are especially strong.
rows.anchor: ولما كانت عنايته بالله أتم لما له من عظيم المراقبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The proper middle of the road is the route God will show him without deviation.
rows.anchor: أي عدل ووسط { السبيل * } وهو الطريق الذي يطلعه عليها من غير اعوجاج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses reaches the watering place intending to drink; it is the water from which shepherds draw.
rows.anchor: حضور من يشرب { ماء مدين } اي الذي يستقي منها الرعاء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He finds a large group tending livestock, a powerful crowd that occupies and dominates access to the water.
rows.anchor: جماعة كثيرة هم أهل لأن يقصدوا ويقصدوا , فلذلك هم عالون غالبون على الماء

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The object of ‘watering’ is omitted because the action itself is what matters in the description.
rows.anchor: وحذف المفعول لأنه غير مراد , والمراد الفعل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The two women stand nearer the approach to the water than the group, and their designation as women points to their noble character revealed later.
rows.anchor: بذلك لما جعل لهما سبحانه من المروءة ومكارم الأخلاق

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tadhūdān means they restrain, prevent, and drive away their thirsty sheep to keep them from mixing with other flocks.
rows.anchor: وهو الكف والمنع والطرد وارتكاب أخف الضررين

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ compassion concerns the acts of restraining and withholding water, not the fact that the animals are sheep.
rows.anchor: فإن رحمته عليه الصلاة والسلام لم تكن لكون المذود والمسقي غنما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh responds after Moses’ exhortations and warnings, once the great signs have been shown.
rows.anchor: جوابا لهذا الترغيب والترهيب بعد الإعذار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s recurring tactic is to keep his people from believing for a while whenever Moses shows a proof, exploiting their foolish preference for falsehood.
rows.anchor: كلما أظهر موسى عليه الصلاةوالسلام برهانا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He honors the nobles in his address to win their hearts.
rows.anchor: أي الأشراف , معظما لهم استجلابا لقلوبهم

words: مَا عَلِمْتُ لَكُم مِّنْ إِلَٰهٍ غَيْرِى
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh frames the denial as a lack of knowledge to appear fair, while using it to create doubt despite knowing Moses has the truth.
rows.anchor: إظهارا للنصفة , وأنه ما قصد غشهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Haman is Pharaoh’s minister, and the clay is made into bricks for building.
rows.anchor: { يا هامان } وهو وزيره

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh attributes the firing to himself to signal that it must be done.
rows.anchor: أضاف الإيقاد إليه إعلاما بأنه لا بد منه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: A ṣarḥ is a tall structure that reaches toward the sky.
rows.anchor: { صرحا } اي بناء عايا يتاخم السماء

rows.speaker: الطبري
rows.claim: Al-Tabari says every flat-roofed building is like a palace.
rows.anchor: قال الطبري : وكل بناء مسطح فهو كالقصر

rows.speaker: الزجاج
rows.claim: Al-Zajjaj defines a ṣarḥ as any broad, elevated building.
rows.anchor: قال الزجاج : كل بناء متسع مرتفع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Aṭṭaliʿ means that Pharaoh will undertake the effort of climbing.
rows.anchor: { لعلي أطلع } أي أتكلف الطلوع

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh pretends that he can seek Moses’ God in the sky if the claim is true, while being certain otherwise and using the project to delay belief.
rows.anchor: إله موسى } اي الذي يدعوا إليه , فإنه ليس في الرض أحد بهذا الوصف

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The pronoun refers to Moses, whom Pharaoh accuses of being a habitual liar.
rows.anchor: أي موسى { من الكاذبين * } أي دأبه ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Taken literally, Pharaoh’s plan exposes his ignorance: he imagines reaching the sky, climbing it, and confronting its maker.
rows.anchor: على حقيقته فلا شيء أثبت شهادة على غفراط جهله وغباوته

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh’s speech successfully turns his people toward arrogant resistance to truth and attachment to falsehood.
rows.anchor: اتبعه تعالى الإشارة غلى أنهم فعلوا ما أراد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their arrogance is marked as unjust; elevation grounded in truth is not blameworthy, while God’s own exaltation is wholly rightful.
rows.anchor: التعبير بالتعريف يدل على أن التعظيم بنوع من الحق ليس كبرا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Pharaoh and his people believed they would not return to God’s judgment, so they dared to commit corruption.
rows.anchor: أي فرعون وقومه ظنا بنوا عليه اعتقادهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The second command to call the partners is delivered mockingly, to humiliate followers who answer anyone’s order.
rows.anchor: اي ثانيا للأتباع تهكما للاستهانة بهم , وأنهم من الذل والصغار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The partners are called theirs because their claim arose only from giving the idols their own wealth, speech, time, and conduct.
rows.anchor: لم يستفيدوا زعمهم أنهم شركاء الله تعالى الله عن ذلك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: They call in desperate confusion, clinging to what cannot help, but the partners do not answer because they cannot perceive or act and are themselves doomed.
rows.anchor: تعللا بما لا يغني , وتمسكا بما يتحقق أنه لا يجدي , لفرط الغلبة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Everyone sees the punishment and knows it will reach them with no one able to prevent it.
rows.anchor: عالمين بأنه مواقعهم لا مانع له عنهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The phrase can express regret that they had no guidance, or mean that guidance in their nature would have saved them, spared them seeing punishment, or kept them from following idols.
rows.anchor: أي يحصل منهم هدى ساعة من الدهر , تأسفا على أمرهم , وتمنيا لخلاصهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The passage turns from the impossibility of rescue without guidance to the coming inquiry about the messengers, after the question about God’s due.
rows.anchor: لا خلاص من ذلك الردى إلا بالهدى , أتبعه الإعلام بأنه لا يمكن أحدا هناك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: On that day no one can fabricate the kind of defense people can produce in this world; the scene is made terrifying and the partners’ helplessness is exposed.
rows.anchor: من إظهار ما لم يكن مكررا لتويل ذلك اليوم وتبشيعه وتعظيمه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The gathered people are fully exposed on one plain, crushed by the crowd, with feet piled over feet and sweat overwhelming them.
rows.anchor: في صعيد واحد , قد أخذ بأنفاسهم الزحام , وتراكبت الأقدام على الأقدام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The question asks them to state clearly what answer they gave the messengers.
rows.anchor: أي أوضحوا أو عينوا جوابكم الذي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because they lacked any truthful basis in response to the messengers’ proofs, their answer can only be silence, as the next verse says.
rows.anchor: لم يكن لهم قدم صدق ولا سابق حق بما أتتهم الرسل به من الحجج

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: After the partners’ helplessness in the Hereafter, the text shows God’s rule in this world by destroying arrogant people who cannot save one another.
rows.anchor: ولما دل على عجزهم في تلك الدار , وعلمهم أن المتصرف في جميع الأقدار

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The general warning about towns ruined for their prosperity is applied to Qarun as a particular example.
rows.anchor: تطبيقا لعموم { وكم أهلكنا من قرية بطرت معيشتها }

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun’s destruction warns those who accuse the Prophet of magic and shows that prophets separate from the wretched even when they are close kin.
rows.anchor: تخويفا لمن كذب النبي صلى الله عليه وسلم , لا سيما من نسبه غلى السحر

words: إِنَّ قَٰرُونَ كَانَ مِن قَوْمِ مُوسَىٰ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God destroyed Qarun and his companions with an unprecedented punishment, though they were Israelites and among Moses’ closest people.
rows.anchor: عذب قارون ومن كان معه بعذاب لم يسبقهم فيه أحد

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Those who boast in gifts must recognize God’s right in what the messengers and scriptures teach; worldly possessions cannot save those who rely on them as if they secured lasting happiness.
rows.anchor: أن الحق لله في كل ما دعت إليه رسله , ونطقت به كتبه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Their worldly dependence resembles the spider that takes a house, a comparison found in the following sūra.
rows.anchor: كما يأتي في التي بعده كمثل العنكبوت اتخذت بيتا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses witnessed Qarun’s rejection and accusation of magic but did not pray against him, since arrogance removed him from the promise to aid the oppressed.
rows.anchor: حين كذبه ونسبه إلى السحر وتكبر عليه , فلم يسأل الله تعالى فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun’s punishment resembles Pharaoh’s in concealing them from sight: Pharaoh was submerged in liquid, while Qarun was buried in solid earth, demonstrating God’s power.
rows.anchor: من جنس ما عذب به فرعون في الصورة من حيث إنه تغييب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses selected a witness from each Israelite tribe; the account continues in the next segment.
rows.anchor: من كل سبط من أسباط بني إسرائيل شهيدا من عصبهم

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun is called Qorach in the Torah.
rows.anchor: { إن قارون } ويسمى في التوراة قورح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun was one of the believers in Moses and belonged to the people promised divine favor after oppression.
rows.anchor: أنه كان من الذين آمنوا به

rows.speaker: ابن عباس
rows.claim: Ibn Abbas, as cited by Abu Hayyan and others, says Qarun was Moses’ cousin.
rows.anchor: عن ابن عباس رضي الله عنهما

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Qarun transgresses by despising his people because of wealth, cutting his bonds with them and joining Pharaoh’s party; this moves him from favor and trust into ruin and betrayal.
rows.anchor: تجاوز الحد في احتقارهم بما خولناه فيه من هذا الحطام المتلاشي

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The preposition ʿalā signals overbearing and marks Qarun’s willful departure from proper conduct.
rows.anchor: المقتضية للاستعلاء تنبيها على خروجها عن أصلها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Kunūz are buried and stored wealth, in addition to visible property ready to spend on needs.
rows.anchor: الأموال المدفونة المدخرة , فضلا عن الظاهرة التي هي بصدد الإنفاق منه

words: مَآ إِنَّ مَفَاتِحَهُۥ لَتَنُوٓءُ بِٱلْعُصْبَةِ أُو۟لِى ٱلْقُوَّةِ
rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The treasure keys are so heavy that a strong, mutually supporting group strains under them; the layered wording conveys wealth beyond anyone of Qarun’s rank.
rows.anchor: وفي المبالغة بالتعبير بالكنوز والمفاتيح والنوء والعصبة الموصوفة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The keys open the locks behind the doors of the places where Qarun’s treasure was stored.
rows.anchor: مفتاح الأغلاق التي هو مدفون فيما وراء أبوابها

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Tanūʾ means to tilt or strain with effort under a heavy burden.
rows.anchor: أي تميل بجهد ومشقة لثقلها

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi explains that nuʾ is a star setting from view, and gives both senses of carrying a load: rising under its weight and being tilted by it.
rows.anchor: قال الرازي : والنوء : الكوكب مال عن العين عند الغروب

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The next phrase identifies the time when Qarun’s people spoke and introduces the cause of his transgression.
rows.anchor: ولما ذكر بغيه , ذكر وقته , والوقت قد يكون واسعا

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Moses’ tribal witnesses were told to bring proof about the priesthood; Aaron’s staff blossomed while theirs did not, showing that God decides priesthood and all affairs.
rows.anchor: وقال لهم : هاتوا برهانكم فيها , فعلموا بإبراق عصا هاورن عليه الصلاة والسلام

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Although the verse attributes the counsel to Qarun’s whole people, only some spoke; either the rest agreed or only the righteous count as people.
rows.anchor: وساغت نسبة القول للكل وإن كان القائل البعض

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The warning targets joy in perishable wealth that settles into the heart and burns into arrogance and insolence.
rows.anchor: لا تسر سرورا يحفر في قلبك فيتغلغل فيه فيحرقك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Rejoicing in transient possessions shows reliance on them and forgetfulness of the afterlife; it reflects ignorance and poor judgment, leading to arrogance and ruin.
rows.anchor: فإن الفرح بالعرض الزائل يدل على الركون إليه , وذلك يدل على نسيان الآخرة

rows.speaker: الرازي
rows.claim: Al-Razi says rejoicing in what is not worth rejoicing over brings grief that never ends.
rows.anchor: قال الرزاي : ومن فرح بغير مفروح به استجلب حزنا لا انقضاء له

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: God’s perfection is what merits joy; people deeply rejoicing in what perishes reveal low aspirations, and God does not treat them as beloved.
rows.anchor: الذي له صفات الكمال فلا شيء أجل منه , فبه ينبغي أن يفرح

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: The text implies an additional call to renounce worldly attachment because abstaining from this joy leads to asceticism and nearness to God.
rows.anchor: ترك الفرح سببا للزهد , وهو سبب القرب إلى الله , كان كأن قيل

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Ibtaghi commands Qarun to seek with strenuous effort.
rows.anchor: أي اطلب طلبا تجهد نفسك فيه

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He should use God’s wealth to pursue the Hereafter by spending it in ways God loves; this pursuit gives wealth life and reminds him that the world is temporary and all its possessions perish.
rows.anchor: أي الملك الأعظم الذي له الأمر كله من هذه الأموال حال تمكنك

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: He may enjoy lawful food, clothing, marriage, and homes, but without excess or vanity that abandons fairness.
rows.anchor: بل استعمل المباحات من المآكل والملابس والمناكح والمساكن

rows.speaker: علي
rows.claim: Ali explains one’s worldly share as health, strength, vitality, and wealth that can be used to seek the Hereafter.
rows.anchor: وعن علي رضي الله عنه : ولا تنس صحتك وقوتك ونشاطك وغناك أن تطلب به الآخرة

rows.speaker: author
rows.claim: Because human appetite grows once a little worldly enjoyment is allowed, Qarun’s people add further counsel to restrain his greed.
rows.anchor: فإذا أذن لها من الدنيا في نقير جعلته أكبر كبير
